plan.topic: Your tirzepatide pen looks different from someone else's: single-dose pen vs KwikPen vs vial, and why a different device doesn't mean a different medicine
plan.angle: Sentence 1 as written. Then: the US tirzepatide labels list more than one device, naming only those printed in each PI's How Supplied section. Add 'In Australia, Mounjaro comes as a KwikPen' (verified via the TGA/medsinfo consumer leaflet). Add the UK only if the UK SmPC or patient leaflet confirms it. Myth line: 'A different device doesn't mean a different medicine: the active ingredient is tirzepatide in each. Your dose is set by your prescriber, and it can differ from someone else's.' No mention of doses, clicks, strengths, leftover medicine or getting extra doses from a pen. Then: each device has its own steps, so follow the leaflet in your box and ask a pharmacist to show you. 'Don't swap devices on your own.' Then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Cite each IFU at its own URL.

It also serves UK/AU viewers whose packs differ. | fact-check: A good reassurance topic, but there's a real safety edge. The KwikPen is a multi-dose pen and the others are single-dose, so device talk can slide into dose, click or extra-dose talk, which is self-titration territory. Checked: in Australia, Mounjaro comes as a KwikPen (the TGA-listed 'Mounjaro KwikPen' consumer leaflet lists tirzepatide as the active ingredient). The UK KwikPen still has to be checked against the UK SmPC or patient leaflet, or dropped. For the US, don't promise in advance that three devices are listed: name only what each PI's How Supplied section prints. The myth line also needs care. A different device isn't a different medicine, but a friend's dose may well be different from yours. Don't let 'not stronger' suggest that every pen holds the same dose.

script.hook_pattern: result-first: sentence 1 gives the reassurance up front (a different tirzepatide pen from a friend's doesn't mean a different medicine), so the answer is the hook. The payoffs follow: US Zepbound label devices (single-dose pen, single-dose vial, four-dose KwikPen), then the Australian four-dose KwikPen, then the myth flip with the dose caveat in the same line. After that, one practical safety scene: follow your box leaflet, get pens only from a pharmacy on your prescription, never share one. The close is the disclaimer, then the don't-swap line, then a loop line that runs back into sentence 1. Nothing about clicks, strengths, leftover medicine or extra doses.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe to ship. I opened all three sources and they say what the script claims:
- **Zepbound label (DailyMed, revised 28 Aug 2026):** lists a single-dose pen, a single-dose vial and a multi-dose KwikPen with four doses per pen. Section 5.10 says "Never share ZEPBOUND KwikPen between patients, even if the pen needle is changed."
- **Mounjaro label (revised 27 Aug 2026):** has the same never-share warning.
- **Australian Mounjaro KwikPen leaflet (prepared September 2026):** confirms tirzepatide as the active ingredient and "4 fixed doses" per pen.

Safety and rules:
- The narration avoids strengths, clicks, leftover medicine and dosing.
- The dose caveat sits in the same scene as the "same ingredient" point (s5).
- The don't-swap line and the required Shorts closing are present. There's no subscribe line and no "link in the description" line.
- Spoken words come to about 154, inside the 160 limit and the standard 135–160 arm.

I found three wording problems. None of them makes a claim wrong. Apply the fixes before render.

issues.claim: Get pens only from a pharmacy, on your prescription.
issues.problem: This is our own safety tip, not a label sentence, but the scene tags it to the Zepbound and Mounjaro labels. Our rule: own tips get no source tag. The labels do support 'never share', and the separate instructions for each device support 'each device has its own steps'.
issues.fix: Keep the zepbound-pi and mounjaro-pi tags only for 'Each device has its own steps, so follow the leaflet in your box' and 'And never share one.' Add a scene note: "'Get pens only from a pharmacy, on your prescription' = InforMed safety tip, untagged." Don't show any label citation next to the pharmacy item on screen.

issues.claim: ZEPBOUND / ZEPBOUND KWIKPEN (tirzepatide) injection ... sections 3, 5 (Never Share a Zepbound KwikPen Between Patients) ...
issues.problem: The DailyMed listing title is 'ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, solution'. The never-share warning is in section 5.10, not section 5 as a whole.
issues.fix: Retitle to: "ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, solution, US Prescribing Information (DailyMed): sections 3 (Dosage Forms and Strengths), 5.10 (Never Share a ZEPBOUND KwikPen Between Patients), 16 (How Supplied) and 17 (Patient Counseling Information)". Drop section 11 if no scene relies on it.

issues.problem: A muted viewer may read 'pen' as any pen. The narration says single-dose pen and single-dose vial, so the on-screen text is less specific than the narration.
issues.fix: Change to: "US Zepbound label: single-dose pen, single-dose vial, 4-dose KwikPen"
